title: An analog ac voltage amplifier based on a single straintronic magnetic tunnel junction
authors: Cael Johnson, Rahnuma Rahman, Supriyo Bandyopadhyay
abstract: Magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) are known for their digital applications (memory and logic). A special class of them called "straintronic" magnetic tunnel junctions (s-MTJ) has lately emerged as a potential platform for analog applications because their conductance can be varied continuously with mechanical strain generated with a gate voltage. The conductance versus gate voltage (transfer) characteristic always has a linear region and that can be leveraged for a variety of analog applications. Here, we discuss one such application, namely analog voltage amplification. If the s-MTJ's gate voltage is fixed around the midpoint of the linear region and a small ac voltage is superimposed on it, then the ac voltage can be amplified without distortion as long as its amplitude is small enough to avoid gate voltage excursion beyond the linear region. Unlike a transistor-based voltage amplifier whose amplification is determined solely by the transistor's internal parameters - namely the transconductance and Early resistance - here the amplification can be varied by an external power supply voltage. We examine the maximum allowed amplitude and frequency of input signal for distortion-free amplification by modeling the magnetization dynamics and derive an expression for the amplification.
summary: This paper proposes using a straintronic magnetic tunnel junction (s-MTJ) as a highly tunable analog AC voltage amplifier. The device's gain is uniquely dependent on an external supply voltage, offering advantages over fixed-gain transistors. By analyzing the magnetization dynamics, the authors derive the amplification characteristics and suggest structural modifications to enhance performance.
main_problem: To demonstrate a novel analog AC voltage amplifier utilizing the unique properties of straintronic magnetic tunnel junctions (s-MTJs).
main_result: The device exhibits linear amplification whose gain is tunable by an external power supply voltage, unlike traditional transistors.
method: The authors modeled the magnetization dynamics and derived the amplification factor based on superimposing a small AC voltage onto a DC bias point within the s-MTJ's linear conductance regime.
model_or_system: The system is a single straintronic magnetic tunnel junction (s-MTJ), whose resistance depends on the magnetization angle ($\phi$) and can be continuously tuned by an external gate voltage ($V_G$).
key_observables: Output voltage $	ilde{V}$, amplification factor $A$, conductance swing, and maximum allowed AC input amplitude.
important_parameters: The proportionality constant $\kappa$ (slope of linear conductance vs. $V_G$), the supply voltage $V_S$, and the ferromagnetic resonance frequency (GHz range).
main_assumptions: The amplification remains distortion-free only if the AC gate voltage excursion stays within the established linear region, and the signal frequency must be low enough relative to the magnetization dynamics.
figures_summary: Figure 5 illustrates the relationship between output voltage and input gate voltage swing, showing the derived linear amplification formula.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical basis of s-MTJs for analog applications by noting their linear conductance region. It then models the AC amplification process, deriving the gain expression, and finally discusses methods to improve performance by modifying device geometry or material properties.
why_interesting: While focused on spintronics/electronics, the underlying physics involves non-linear dynamics (LLGL simulations) coupled to an external control parameter ($V_G$), which touches upon concepts of parametric amplification and controlled quantum/classical response relevant to open quantum systems.
